title: Complete Form I-9 · Section 1
summary: The employee completes and signs Section 1 no later than the first day of work for pay.
action: Provide the current Form I-9 instructions and acceptable-document lists. Review Section 1 for completeness; the employee may complete it after accepting the job offer.
reason: This profile represents an ordinary new paid hire in the United States.

title: Review documents · Section 2
summary: Complete employer review within three business days after the first day of paid work. A job lasting fewer than three days has a first-day deadline.
action: Review acceptable documentation and complete and sign Section 2. Let the employee choose the acceptable documents. Follow official guidance for receipts or authorized remote examination; this app does not examine documents.
reason: Employer review is part of Form I-9 for the ordinary new paid hire in this profile.

title: Arrange secure I-9 retention
summary: Keep required Forms I-9 while employees work for you, and apply the retention period after employment ends.
action: Use a separate secure record system for actual Forms I-9. Review the official retention and storage instructions. Do not upload documents or personal employee information to EasyVerify.
reason: Required I-9 records need a retention process beyond completing this checklist.

title: Create the new-hire E-Verify case
summary: For the ordinary enrolled-employer path, create the case after Form I-9 is complete, no later than the third business day after paid work starts.
action: Create the case in the official E-Verify system. Do not create a case before the employer’s MOU effective date. Review official exceptions, including an employee awaiting an SSN. EasyVerify does not connect to government records.
reason: You selected E-Verify participation and confirmed no FAR E-Verify clause. This is the ordinary new-hire path, not a contractor-specific timeline.

title: Review the FAR E-Verify contract requirements
summary: A confirmed FAR E-Verify clause needs the contractor-specific enrollment, coverage, exception, and timing review.
action: Read your contract and the official contractor guide. Verify the clause, applicable exemptions, covered employees, and enrollment/case timelines with your contracting officer. A generic three-day case deadline is not generated here.
reason: You confirmed a FAR E-Verify clause. Contract-specific rules cannot be resolved from headcount and state alone.

title: Check whether your contract has the FAR clause
summary: Government contracting alone does not resolve E-Verify obligations. Check the actual contract language.
action: Locate the FAR E-Verify clause or ask your contracting officer. Update the profile once you have a confirmed answer. Until then, this app leaves the E-Verify case timeline unresolved.
reason: Your FAR E-Verify clause answer is unknown.

title: Confirm your E-Verify enrollment status
summary: Confirm whether your business participates in E-Verify before applying its case workflow.
action: Check your enrollment records and MOU. Participation is separate from completing Form I-9. Update this profile when confirmed.
reason: Your E-Verify participation answer is unknown.

title: Review California’s additional restrictions
summary: California rules require a separate review. This app does not determine state E-Verify enrollment requirements or restrictions.
action: Review California Labor Code §2814 and other applicable state guidance before using E-Verify. This statutory source has not been independently reviewed in this release; no state-specific legal conclusion is generated.
reason: Your business is in California. Federal checklist results do not resolve state obligations.

title: Check your state’s verification requirements
summary: State-specific rules are not included for this location. The federal checklist is only part of the picture.
action: Consult official state labor and contracting guidance. Do not interpret a federal checklist as confirmation of state compliance.
reason: This release includes federal guidance and a California research link; it does not contain a 50-state rules database.
